screening_method_note: CREATED SD31-W4-INTEGRATE-001, 2026-08-16 (OPEN-ISSUES.md row 48/49): this book gained real content this wave (SD31-E5-F1-001's class_feature cache-gen) but no LICENSE.json compliance artifact was ever created for it -- `tests/sd27_book_license_record_counts.rs`'s own `books_on_disk()` only enumerates books that ALREADY have a LICENSE.json, so this gap was invisible to that guard rather than failing it. The records themselves were genuinely PI-screened inline at write time (cache_gen::class_feature calls pi_screening::classify_field on both name and description plus the declared-PI reader on both fields, per OPEN-ISSUES.md row 48's fix) -- this artifact documents that screening, it does not re-run it. records_processed = 11 (find data/corpus/inner_sea_taverns -mindepth 2 -name '*.json' ! -name LICENSE.json -not -path '*/_parity/*' | wc -l), records_redacted = 0 (real on-disk license==PI-REDACTED count). This is NOT an exhaustive human legal review; it is a bounded substring scan plus the corpus's own declared-PI tokens, and does not prove the absence of PI beyond what that scan can see.
